overall_structure.value: After 60% hot compression at 1150 °C and 1 s^-1 the deformation-zone microstructures differ: zone 1 (difficult deformation) consists of large grains, whereas zones 2 (small deformation) and 3 (large deformation) consist of uniform equiaxed dynamically recrystallized grains that appear coarser than those formed at 1050 °C/1 s^-1. The DRX volume fraction increases with temperature, and the recrystallized grain size grows significantly as temperature rises.

unmapped_findings: Zener-Hollomon parameter for this sample (1150 °C, 1 s^-1): lnZ = 56.62 (Table 1). Table 1 reports lnZ decreasing with increasing T and increasing with strain rate across 900-1150 °C and 0.01-10 s^-1.

Dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the steel Q_p = 669.844 kJ mol^-1, determined from the Arrhenius hyperbolic sine function equation with k1 = 5.135 and k2 = 15.690 and α = 0.00599; this is only an average value over the experimental range because the fitted lines show poor parallelism.

The DRX average grain size of the steel increases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature; the study reports that at 1150 °C and 0.01 s^-1 (not this sample) the grain size exceeds 70 µm, indicating rapid recrystallized grain growth.

Recommended hot-working windows for a fine and uniform grain structure: 950-1000 °C/0.01-0.1 s^-1 and 1050-1100 °C/1-10 s^-1; the 1150 °C/1 s^-1 condition of this sample lies outside these fine-grain windows.

The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material; decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature lowers the peak/flow stress. Peak stress at 1150 °C, 0.01 s^-1 (not this sample) is 53.8 MPa.

No direct numeric peak stress, hardness, tensile or grain-size value is reported for the specific 1150 °C/1 s^-1 condition; only qualitative zone-resolved microstructures (figure_009 panel f) are provided for this sample.

The compression experiments used mica foils with high-temperature lubricants on both end faces to reduce friction and non-uniform deformation; the same batch/composition confirmed reproducibility under identical conditions.
